A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BSD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between appendix sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on image classification, image reconstruction, character prediction and time-series forecasting, including ablations in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds Tiny-ImageNet results, robustness tests, ablations and computational-resource analyses.

M1.justification: The bidirectional architecture, local ReCo objectives, detached interlayer training, RNN formulation and FFT-based generation procedure are retained. Expanded notation and FFT explanations describe the existing method. The conflicting update sign newly printed in Equation (9), discussed under T1, does not establish a coherent procedural revision.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds Tiny-ImageNet classification, and Appendix L adds Gaussian-corrupted CIFAR-10 and SVHN test scenarios. These extend coverage within image classification; the existing image reconstruction, character prediction and forecasting coverage remains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the corresponding original experiments is unchanged. The added experiments reuse existing comparators, including BP and DLL. Newly discussed approaches such as LRA-E, DNI and e-prop are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled batch-size sweeps from 16 to 256, timestep sweeps over 2, 4, 6 and 8, and comparisons with and without batch normalization. New protocols also cover clean-trained models tested with Gaussian noise of standard deviation 0.05, memory profiling at three batch sizes, and operation-based inference-energy estimation. These substantially expand evaluation design without replacing the original protocols.

E4.justification: New appendices investigate batch-size sensitivity, timestep sensitivity, batch normalization, input-noise robustness, inference energy and training/inference memory costs. These address operating conditions and practical tradeoffs absent from v1. Existing loss ablations, firing-threshold analysis, weight alignment and t-SNE studies are retained, with some relocated.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain their four-random-seed averaging statements and uncertainty values. The added tables report point estimates without introducing new run-count disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Original numerical scores in Tables 1–7 are retained, while Tables 8–18 add substantial results. Examples include Tiny-ImageNet accuracy of 35.34% for BSD versus 41.07% for BP and 17.10% for DLL, an estimated 85.5% inference-energy reduction versus the ANN, and training memory of 5034 versus 3324 MB for BSD versus BP at batch size 128. Table 1 also changes Predictive Coding's plausibility assessment from satisfying C1–C3 to satisfying only C2.

T1.justification: Appendices K and N add an operation-based energy model and complexity analysis, including BSD's additional O(LB^2D) affinity-computation term. Existing gradient derivations remain unchanged. New Equation (9) introduces a mathematical inconsistency: it adds the gradient while calling the operation gradient descent, whereas Algorithm 1 retains subtraction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: bidirectional spike-based distillation, satisfaction of five biological-plausibility criteria, and performance comparable to backpropagation across several architectures and tasks. Added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations linking batch-size dependence to negative-sample diversity, noise robustness to the combined discriminative and generative objectives, and training-memory overhead to the second pathway and affinity matrix. It also distinguishes inference efficiency from training costs. The existing architectural limitations are retained, moving from Appendix G to R.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository link and availability statement instead of v1's promise of public release upon acceptance, and identifies an RTX 2080 Ti for resource profiling. It clarifies CNN upsampling as reversing pooling. Most original implementation settings remain unchanged, and Appendix M largely expands FFT details already present in Appendix E.2.4.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens research positioning through attention and residual SNNs, local-error learning, feedback alignment, predictive coding/LRA-E, synthetic gradients and e-prop. It adds the corresponding references and removes v1's blanket statement that the method uniquely satisfies established biological constraints.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with localized terminology and notation corrections, expanded explanations, author/contact updates and acknowledgments. Former Appendices F.4 and F.5 become G and H, while limitations and the LLM disclosure move to R and S. The reproducibility statement introduces an unresolved 'Appendix ??' reference.

P2.justification: Tables 8–18 add substantial displays of benchmark, robustness, sensitivity, layer-wise energy and memory comparisons. Figures 3 and 7 are restyled, including labels and plotting layout, while presenting retained analyses. Existing figures and tables are preserved and reflowed rather than removed.

improvement.justification: The added robustness tests, sensitivity studies and resource profiling make BSD's operating conditions and computational tradeoffs better supported than in v1. Expanded related work and explicit code-access information also help readers assess and reproduce the work. These gains are tempered by absent uncertainty reporting for the new studies, the new update-sign contradiction between Equation (9) and Algorithm 1, and the broken appendix reference. The net improvement is useful but limited.
